summary: Tenant-aware SIEM entity crosswalk, deterministic pseudonymization, CSV deliverable and security evidence bundle
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a nightly CSV deliverable that contains a tenant-scoped SIEM event crosswalk mapping original user identifiers to deterministic pseudonyms. Impact: Compliance deadline for financial regulator in 7 days; customer cannot proceed with audit without deliverable. Environment: Redwood Private VPC deployment in us-east with dedicated audit-export pipeline.

They need: 1) per-event CSV with columns (event_timestamp, tenant_id, original_id_hash, pseudo_id, event_type, payload_reference) 2) deterministic pseudonymization algorithm (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt) with rotatable KEK, 3) signed delivery manifest with RFC3161 timestamps and SHA256 checksums, 4) SFTP drop with presigned object-lock and retention metadata, 5) a short security evidence bundle describing cryptographic controls, KMS key lifecycle, and sample pseudonymization code snippet.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer ran on-demand export job via Console -> Exports -> New Export using 'tenant=maplebank' and 'window=2026-03-09T00:00:00Z/2026-03-09T23:59:59Z'
Export job completed but CSV contained unhashed identifiers for ~2% of rows due to null-handling bug
Customer attached sample CSV rows and asked for signed manifest and attestation for retention policy
logs: Export job id: export-20260309-42. Server log snippet: 2026-03-09T02:14:21Z INFO export started; 2026-03-09T02:14:25Z WARN null identifier encountered for event id e-9f34; 2026-03-09T02:14:25Z INFO substituted fallback 'UNKNOWN' into original_id field; 2026-03-09T02:14:29Z INFO export completed rows=182,345 checksum=sha256:ab12...ef34. See S3 object s3://private-exports/maplebank/2026-03-09/export-42.csv (internal access).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: null-handling path bypassed pseudonymization routine when original identifier missing; code path created 'UNKNOWN' literal leading to unhashed field in CSV
Checked export pipeline code in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/exports PR #2389 referenced for null-sentinel change
Verified KMS key policy: customer-kek-01 has rotation schedule and is accessible by export-service principal
Export manifest generator currently runs as last step; manifest generation uses file bytes to compute checksum but did not verify pseudonymization compliance
Requested sample of affected rows from customer and the full manifest; asked infra to provide object-lock metadata for the S3 drop
Attached traces: link to datadog dashboard (https://dd.redwood.internal/d/exports/export-42) and query for null-id occurrences
comments: Ava Martinez (Customer): 'We need this by 2026-03-13 EOD for our regulator. Attaching sample CSV and questionnaire.'

Ravi Patel (Support): 'Acknowledged. Triage'ing as P1. I've started collection of logs and requested infra to freeze the export object lock for the bucket. Can you confirm whether the sample includes PII? If so we'll redact in transit.'

Ravi Patel (Support): 'Found code path: export/transformer/null_sentinel branch bypasses pseudonymize_id() when id == null. Raising INT issue for fix. In the meantime we can run a remediation job to reprocess the exported file and replace original_id with HMAC-based pseudo_id.'
SRE (internal): 'Reserved ephemeral capacity to run reprocess job. Need customer approval for reprocessing and a window for maintenance.'
Ava Martinez (Customer): 'Approve reprocess; needs to be non-disruptive and audit-proof. Also require signed RFC3161 manifest and retention attestation.'
resolution_notes: Workaround: ran reprocessing job to pseudonymize 'original_id' using HMAC-SHA256 with tenant salt retrieved from KMS (customer-kek-01). Generated new CSV: export-42-reprocessed.csv. Manifest generated with SHA256 checksums and RFC3161 timestamp from timestamper.redwood.com. Delivery: placed in SFTP drop sftp://exports.redwood.com/maplebank/2026-03-09/ with presigned object lock metadata and retention headers. Provided customer with reproducible script (python snippet) and attestation PDF signed by support manager. Postmortem action: created INT-5490 to add null-sentinel handling test and unit tests for pseudonymization; PR merged in exports repo; scheduled rollout to prod on 2026-03-15. Customer verified and closed the ticket with confirmation of receipt and audit acceptance.
